cells.tense: The exchange is running even now, and you have the pen in your hand.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've decided is fair and keep that decision for the day, even when a counter-argument shows up.
cells.core:
Fairness arrives at the same time the thing does. Something comes in, and you feel its weight without running the numbers — who gave, who owes, what actually fits. That knowing stays quiet because it doesn't need defending. What arrives meets you, and you meet it, and the exchange stays open.

Watch what happens when something new comes through the door this week. You can say the fairness holds in one sentence rather than argue the whole case, and the balance doesn't need a guard standing over it. It needs you to keep walking with it, letting what is next arrive at the pace it is arriving at.
cells.sheetLine: The balance holds before the counting starts.
cells.place: At the threshold where what was outside arrives

cells.tense: You will be running the tally before the thing has even arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one exchange this week where nothing is owed and stay out of the math — no more here, no more here, this one left alone.
cells.core:
You can see the unfairness coming before it lands. A conversation hasn't started and the tally is already traced — who owes what, what gets accepted, what gets remembered. Somewhere ahead is a moment when it all gets set right, and you're living there, so the reckoning is decided before anything new has a chance to enter.

That readiness costs you the arrivals themselves. What's coming in gets measured before it's arrived, and there's no room left for exchange, only settlement. The tally is real, and what you've noticed isn't wrong. Try one where you sit down without the math and let the other person fill it in. The tallies you keep pre-written will still be there tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You're settling accounts before they come due.
cells.place: At the threshold where what was outside arrives

cells.tense: You give without claiming your share, and your share stays at the door.
cells.ask: Ask one person for one specific thing you want this week — out loud, plainly, no preface — and let the yes or no land either way.
cells.core:
The exchange runs one direction for you now. You offer, you don't ask, and what's owed you stays uncollected. The ask goes out and lands on no one's ear, so nothing comes back your way. Something arriving for you stops at the threshold while you wait to see whether it's safe to take.

Standing where you are now, fairness can start small and stay small: one ask, one specific thing, no case built around it. That gives what's arriving somewhere to land. You don't have to want a lot. One claim, said plainly, is how the exchange begins to run both ways again.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking, and the door is still open.

cells.tense: You are already weighing what comes in, and you'd describe it as simply reacting.
cells.ask: Say once, out loud, that you're keeping score about one thing, and name the thing without arguing the case.
cells.core:
There's a tally running in you and it has been for a while — a running count of who came through and who didn't. You'd call it being realistic. It's yours: it shapes how you answer the phone, what you bring up, how you sit in the room.

The weighing is real work and it's doing it without your name on it. That's the whole trouble and the whole fix. Naming one entry doesn't mean acting on it, doesn't mean anyone hears it, doesn't require deciding who was right. Just say the count is there and you're the one keeping it. The tally gets easier to hold once you've claimed you're holding it.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping score and calling it just noticing.
